I reviewed the whole file (lines 1–41). I also read SemidirectProductTopology.lean, which defines the product topology on the semidirect product and the continuity lemmas for it. In IntegralLatticePowerIndex.lean I read the definitions and lemmas for `latticePowerHom`, `integralSemidirectPowerMap`, its injectivity, its range, and its finite index. In FreeAbelianDuality.lean I read the definition of `IntegralLatticeGroup`. The theorem `integralSemidirectPowerMap_isClosedEmbedding` has hypotheses `0 < m` and an arbitrary homomorphism ρ into `MulAut L`. Those hypotheses are consistent and non-vacuous.

The `m = 0` case is correctly excluded. There the map is not injective when n > 0, because `latticePowerHom` becomes the trivial map. Without `hm` the claim would be false, so the hypothesis is a needed condition, not a restriction that empties the statement.

The claimed conclusion is `IsClosedEmbedding`, and it matches the section title "finite-index power subgroup is closed". The proof shows the range is the preimage under `right` of the range of `latticePowerHom`. `IntegralLatticeGroup n` is `Multiplicative (Fin n → ℤ)`, which should be discrete since it is a finite product of discrete ℤ. The proof uses that discreteness (`continuous_of_discreteTopology`, `isClosed_discrete`). I did not locate the instance that supplies the discrete topology, and the file compiles. The topology on the semidirect product is deliberately the product topology and does not depend on the action being continuous. For this embedding and closedness statement that is sufficient and not misleading. I found no vacuity or mismatch with the documented purpose.
